body.name: add
body.definition: add(x, y, filter = false), x + y
body.description: Adds two or more inputs element wise. Set filter=true to treat NaNs as 0 before summing.

body.name: multiply
body.description: Multiplies two or more inputs element wise. Set filter=true to treat NaNs as 0 before multiplication

body.name: sign
body.description:
Returns the sign of a number: +1 for positive, -1 for negative, and 0 for zero. If the input is NaN, returns NaN.

Input: Value of 7 instruments at day t: (2, -3, 5, 6, 3, NaN, -10)
Output: (1, -1, 1, 1, 1, NaN, -1)

body.name: subtract
body.description: Subtracts inputs left to right: x ? y ? … Supports two or more inputs. Set filter=true to treat NaNs as 0 before subtraction.

body.name: pasteurize
body.description:
Set to NaN if x is INF or if the underlying instrument is not in the Alpha universe. This operator may help reduce outliers.

Input: Value of 7 instruments at day t: (2, 3, 5, INF, 3, 8, 10), where value 10 does not belong in Alpha universe
Output: (2, 3, 5, NaN, 3, 8, NaN)

body.name: log
body.description: Calculates the natural logarithm of the input value. Commonly used to transform data that has positive values.

body.name: purify
body.description: Clear infinities (+inf, -inf) by replacing with NaN

body.name: arc_tan
body.description: This operator does inverse tangent of input

body.name: max
body.description: Maximum value of all inputs. At least 2 inputs are required

body.name: abs
body.description: Returns the absolute value of a number, removing any negative sign.

body.name: sigmoid
body.description: Returns 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

body.name: divide
body.description: x / y

body.name: min
body.description: Minimum value of all inputs. At least 2 inputs are required

body.name: tanh
body.description: Hyperbolic tangent of x

body.name: nan_out
body.description: If x < lower or x > upper return NaN, else return x. At least one of "lower", "upper" is required

body.name: signed_power
body.description: x raised to the power of y such that final result preserves sign of x

body.name: round
body.description: Round input to closest integer.

body.name: sqrt
body.description: Returns the non negative square root of x. Equivalent to power(x, 0.5); for signed roots use signed_power(x, 0.5).

body.name: reverse
body.description: - x

body.name: power
body.description: x ^ y

body.name: densify
body.description: Converts a grouping field of many buckets into lesser number of only available buckets so as to make working with grouping fields computationally efficient

body.name: floor
body.description: Nearest smaller integer

body.name: or
body.description: Returns 1 if either input is true (either input1 or input2 has a value of 1), otherwise it returns 0.

body.name: and
body.description: Returns 1 ('true') if both inputs are 1 ('true'). Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

body.name: not
body.description: Returns the logical negation of x. Returns 0 when x is 1 (‘true’) and 1 when x is 0 (‘false’).

body.name: is_nan
body.description: If (input == NaN) return 1 else return 0

body.name: is_not_nan
body.description: If (input != NaN) return 1 else return 0

body.name: less
body.description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 is a smaller than input2. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

body.name: equal
body.description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 and input2 are the same. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

body.name: greater
body.description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 is a larger than input2. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

body.name: is_finite
body.description: If (input NaN or input == INF) return 0, else return 1

body.name: if_else
body.description: The if_else operator returns one of two values based on a condition. If the condition is true, it returns the first value; if false, it returns the second value.

body.name: not_equal
body.description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 and input2 are different numbers. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

body.name: less_equal
body.description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 is a smaller or the same as input2. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

body.name: greater_equal
body.description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 is a larger or the same as input2. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

body.name: ts_corr
body.description: Calculates the Pearson correlation between two variables, x and y, over the past d days, showing how closely they move together.

body.name: ts_zscore
body.description: Calculates the Z-score of a time series, showing how far today's value is from the recent average, measured in standard deviations. Useful for standardizing and comparing values over time.

body.name: ts_returns
body.description: Returns the relative change in the x value

body.name: ts_product
body.description: Returns the product of the values of x over the past d days. Useful for calculating geometric means and compounding returns or growth rates.

body.name: ts_std_dev
body.description: Calculates the standard deviation of a data series x over the past d days, measuring how much the values deviate from their mean during that period.

body.name: ts_backfill
body.description: Replaces missing (NaN) values in a time series with the most recent valid value from a specified lookback window, improving data coverage and reducing risk from missing data.

body.name: days_from_last_change
body.description: Calculates the number of days since the last change in the value of a given variable.

body.name: last_diff_value
body.description: Returns the most recent value of x from the past d days that is different from the current value of x.

body.name: ts_scale
body.description: Scales a time series to a 0–1 range based on its minimum and maximum values over a specified period, with an optional constant shift.

body.name: ts_entropy
body.description: For each instrument, we collect values of input in the past d days and calculate the probability distribution then the information entropy via a histogram as a result

body.name: ts_step
body.description: Returns a counter of days, incrementing by one each day.

body.name: ts_sum
body.description: Sum values of x for the past d days.

body.name: ts_co_kurtosis
body.description: Returns cokurtosis of y and x for the past d days

body.name: ts_decay_exp_window
body.description: Returns exponential decay of x with smoothing factor for the past d days

body.name: ts_av_diff
body.description: Calculates the difference between a value and its mean over a specified period, ignoring NaN values in the mean calculation. In short, it returns x – ts_mean(x, d) with NaNs ignored.

body.name: ts_kurtosis
body.description: Returns kurtosis of x for the last d days

body.name: ts_mean
body.description: Calculates the simple average (mean) value of a variable x over the past d days.

body.name: ts_min_max_diff
body.description: Returns x - f * (ts_min(x, d) + ts_max(x, d)). If not specified, by default f = 0.5

body.name: ts_arg_max
body.description: Returns the number of days since the maximum value occurred in the last d days of a time series. If today's value is the maximum, returns 0; if it was yesterday, returns 1, and so on.

body.name: ts_min_max_cps
body.description: Returns (ts_min(x, d) + ts_max(x, d)) - f * x. If not specified, by default f = 2

body.name: ts_rank
body.description: Ranks the value of a variable for each instrument over a specified number of past days, returning the rank of the current value (optionally adjusted by a constant). Useful for normalizing time-series data and highlighting relative performance over time.

body.name: ts_ir
body.description: Return information ratio ts_mean(x, d) / ts_std_dev(x, d)

body.name: ts_delay
body.description: Returns the value of a variable x from d days ago. Use this operator to access historical data points by specifying the desired time lag in days.

body.name: ts_theilsen
body.description: Theil Sen slope estimator of inputs for the past n days.

body.name: hump_decay
body.description: This operator helps to ignore the values that changed too little corresponding to previous ones

body.name: ts_weighted_decay
body.description: Instead of replacing today's value with yesterday's as in ts_decay(x, 1), it assigns weighted average of today's and yesterday's values with weight on today's value being k and yesterday's being (1-k)

body.name: ts_quantile
body.description: Calculates the ts_rank of the input and transforms it using the inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile function) of a specified probability distribution (default: Gaussian/normal). This helps to normalize or reshape the distribution of your data over a rolling window.

body.name: ts_count_nans
body.description: Counts the number of missing (NaN) values in a data series over a specified number of days.

body.name: ts_covariance
body.description: Calculates the covariance between two time-series variables, y and x, over the past d days. Useful for measuring how two variables move together within a specified historical window.

body.name: ts_co_skewness
body.description: Returns coskewness of y and x for the past d days

body.name: ts_min_diff
body.description: Returns x - ts_min(x, d)

body.name: ts_decay_linear
body.description: Applies a linear decay to time-series data over a set number of days, smoothing the data by averaging recent values and reducing the impact of older or missing data.

body.name: ts_moment
body.description: Returns K-th central moment of x for the past d days

body.name: ts_arg_min
body.description: Returns the number of days since the minimum value occurred in a time series over the past d days. If today's value is the minimum, returns 0; if it was yesterday, returns 1, and so on.

body.name: ts_regression
body.description: Returns various parameters related to regression function

body.name: ts_skewness
body.description: Return skewness of x for the past d days

body.name: ts_max_diff
body.description: Returns x - ts_max(x, d)

body.name: kth_element
body.description: Returns the K-th value from a time series by looking back over a specified number of (‘d’) days, with the option to ignore certain values. Commonly used for backfilling missing data.

body.name: hump
body.description: Limits amount and magnitude of changes in input (thus reducing turnover)

body.name: ts_delta
body.description: Calculates the difference between a value and its delayed version over a specified period. Useful for measuring changes or momentum in time-series data.

body.name: ts_poly_regression
body.description: Returns y - Ey, where Ey = x + x^2 + ... + x^k over d days; k must be specified as a keyword argument

body.name: ts_target_tvr_decay
body.description: Tune "ts_decay" to have a turnover equal to a certain target, with optimization weight range between lambda_min, lambda_max

body.name: ts_target_tvr_delta_limit
body.description: Tune "ts_delta_limit" to have a turnover equal to a certain target with optimization weight range between lambda_min, lambda_max. Also, please be aware of the scaling for x and y. Besides setting y as adv20 or volume related data, you can also set y as a constant.

body.name: ts_target_tvr_hump
body.description: Tune "hump" to have a turnover equal to a certain target with optimization weight range between lambda_min, lambda_max.

body.name: winsorize
body.description: Winsorize limits values in a data to within a specified number of standard deviations from the mean, reducing the impact of extreme outliers.

body.name: rank
body.description: Ranks the values of the input x among all instruments, returning numbers evenly spaced between 0.0 and 1.0. Useful for normalizing data and reducing the impact of outliers.

body.name: regression_proj
body.description: Conducts the cross-sectional regression on the stocks with Y as target and X as the independent variable

body.name: zscore
body.description: Z-score is a numerical measurement that describes a value's relationship to the mean of a group of values. Z-score is measured in terms of standard deviations from the mean

body.name: scale
body.description: Scales the input so that the sum of absolute values across all instruments equals a specified book size. Allows separate scaling for long and short positions using optional parameters.

body.name: normalize
body.description: Centers a daily cross section by subtracting the market mean; optionally divide by the cross sectional standard deviation and clamp the result to [?limit, +limit]. NaNs are ignored in mean/std.

body.name: rank_gmean_amean_diff
body.description: Operator returns difference of geometric mean and arithmetic mean of cross sectional rank of inputs

body.name: quantile
body.description: Ranks and shifts a vector of Alpha values, then applies a chosen statistical distribution (gaussian, cauchy, or uniform) to reduce outliers. The sigma parameter controls the scale of the output.

body.name: vector_proj
body.description: Returns vector projection of x onto y.

body.name: vec_kurtosis
body.description: Kurtosis of vector field x

body.name: vec_min
body.description: Minimum value form vector field x

body.name: vec_count
body.description: Number of elements in vector field x

body.name: vec_sum
body.description: Calculates the sum of all values in a vector field.

body.name: vec_skewness
body.description: Skewness of vector field x

body.name: vec_max
body.description: Maximum value form vector field x

body.name: vec_avg
body.description: Calculates the mean (average) of all elements in a vector field for each instrument and date, converting vector data to a single matrix value.

body.name: vec_stddev
body.description: Standard Deviation of vector field x

body.name: vec_range
body.description: Difference between maximum and minimum element in vector field x

body.name: bucket
body.definition:
bucket(rank(x), range=“0, 1, 0.1”, skipBoth=False, NaNGroup=False)
or
bucket(rank(x), buckets = “2,5,6,7,10”, skipBoth=False, NaNGroup=False)
body.description: The bucket operator creates custom groups by dividing data into buckets (ranges) based on ranked values of any data field. These buckets can then be used with group operators like group_neutralize, group_rank, group_zscore etc.

body.name: tail
body.description: If (x > lower AND x < upper) return newval, else return x. Lower, upper, newval should be constants

body.name: trade_when
body.description: The trade_when operator changes Alpha values only when a specific condition is met, keeps previous values otherwise, and can close positions by assigning NaN under an exit condition. It is useful for reducing turnover and controlling when trades are executed.

body.name: generate_stats
body.description: The generate_stats() operator calculates Alpha statistics for each day in the IS period. It takes an input of selected Alphas with shape = (A x D x I). It outputs daily statistics for each Alpha with shape = (S x D x A), where S is the number of statistics calculated.

body.name: group_mean
body.description: Calculates the harmonic mean of a data field within each specified group.

body.name: group_rank
body.description: Ranks each element within its group based on the input field, assigning a value between 0.0 and 1.0. This helps compare items within the same group, such as stocks in the same industry.

body.name: group_vector_proj
body.description: Similar to vector_proj(x, y) but x projection to y for each group which can be any classifier such as subindustry, industry, sector, etc.

body.name: group_extra
body.description: Replaces NaN values by their corresponding group means.

body.name: group_backfill
body.description: Fills missing (NaN) values for instruments within the same group by calculating a winsorized mean of all non-NaN values over the past d days. The winsorized mean is computed by trimming extreme values based on a specified standard deviation multiplier (std, default 4.0).

body.name: group_scale
body.description: Normalizes values within each group to a range between 0 and 1, making data comparable across different groups.

body.name: group_count
body.description: Gives the number of instruments in the same group (e.g. sector) which have valid values of x. For example, x=1 gives the number of instruments in each group (without regard for whether any particular field has valid data). This operator improves weight coverage and may help to reduce drawdown risk.

body.name: group_zscore
body.description: Calculates the Z-score of each value within its group, showing how far each value is from the group mean in terms of standard deviations. Useful for comparing values relative to their group.

body.name: group_std_dev
body.description: All elements in group equals to the standard deviation of the group.

body.name: group_sum
body.description: Sum of x for all instruments in the same group.

body.name: group_neutralize
body.description: Neutralizes Alpha values within each specified group by subtracting the group mean from each value. Groups can be industry, sector, country, or any custom grouping.

body.name: group_cartesian_product
body.description: Merge two groups into one group. If originally there are len_1 and len_2 group indices in g1 and g2, there will be len_1 * len_2 indices in the new group.

body.name: combo_a
body.description:
Combines multiple alpha signals into a single weighted output by balancing each alpha's historical return with its variability over the most recent nlength days.

The parameter mode selects one of the several weighted approaches (algo1, algo2, algo3), each of which handles the tradeoff between performance and stability differently.

body.name: inst_pnl
body.description: Generate pnl per instruments. Please note that the use of the inst_pnl() operator in an Alpha Expression is considered as utilizing the pv1 dataset (Price Volume Data for Equity) since it relies on pv1 data for calculations.

body.name: self_corr
body.description: Taking an input matrix of (D x N) with lookback="K", producing an output matrix of (D x N x N), where each output(di, j, k) refers to correlation of input(di-K:di, j) and input(di-K:di, k). Outputs (D x N x N) from the input of (D x N)

body.name: in
body.description: in

body.name: universe_size
body.description: universe_size

body.name: reduce_ir
body.description: IR of values in the array *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_avg
body.description: Average of non-NAN elements of d(..., :). Threshold: Minimum required number of valid (non-nan) values. If there is not enough valid values, then the output is nan. 0 means no limit.threshold (Default: 0) *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_powersum
body.description: Sum of power, sum(power(x, constant)). Threshold: precise, whether calculate power precise if constant greater than 4, default false constant=<integer value>, default:2 *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_max
body.description: Maximum of elements of d(..., :) *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_min
body.description:
Minimum of elements of d(..., :) ***Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. 
If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) 
If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) 
The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_norm
body.description: Absolute sum of number of element of d(..., :) *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_sum
body.description: Sum the number of element of d(..., :) *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_range
body.description: Return the range of values in the array, return NAN if no valid value *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_percentage
body.description: Return the value of percentage in the sorted array: e.g., median value when percentage=0.5. Threshold: percentage="<value between 0 and 1>" (Default: 0.5) *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_skewness
body.description: Skewness of values in the array *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_count
body.description: Count the number of element of d(..., :) > threshold. threshold=<float> *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_kurtosis
body.description:
Kurtosis of values in the array ***Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. 
If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) 
If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) 
The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_choose
body.description: Choose the 'nth' element in the array, return NAN if not found. Threshold: nth="<the Nth element>" (Required) ignoreNan="true|false" (Default: true) *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

body.name: reduce_stddev
body.description: Standard deviation of values in the array. Threshold: Minimum required percentage of valid (non-nan) values. If there is not enough valid values, then the output is NAN. 0 means no limit.threshold (Default: 0) *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).
